Subject: Retention playbook + concrete examples for Aurelia Finance pilot

Hi Kim / Marissa,

Aurelia (pilot deal AU-FT-2345) asked for a short, plain-language runbook that shows: what we store by default (requests, streamed tokens, KV cache, final outputs), examples of customer-visible artifacts, and the erasure steps for each artifact type. They specifically want EU residency clarification and an example purge timeline they can send to their legal/procurement teams.

Can we draft a 1‑page playbook with 3 concrete scenarios (interactive chat, batch ingestion for embeddings, and scheduled report export) and a short "what to expect when you request deletion" section?

I attached the initial notes from the call and their data map (incoming message will include the CSV they promised). Goal is to send a crisp doc back to Alice by EOD CET.

Thanks —
Jonas
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-12T10:21:00+01:00
Subject: Re: Retention playbook + concrete examples for Aurelia Finance pilot

Jonas — thanks. Draft outline below; I can put together the EU-specific bullets and the deletion steps. Quick thoughts:

- "What we keep by default": requests (raw prompts/inputs), model responses (final outputs), streaming fragments (short-term buffer), KV cache (ephemeral runtime cache). Make clear that streaming fragments are not persisted beyond session unless the customer opts into session export.
- Residency: hosted data for this pilot will be stored in our eu-central region; mention dual-write for backups (encrypted, not queryable) and that backups obey the same retention schedule.
- Erasure/Proof: outline that an erasure request triggers immediate logical deletion from live indexes and kickoff of background purge for backups/tombstones with an evidence bundle provided in 7–30 days depending on archive systems.

I'll prepare the scenario examples — interactive chat (demo conversation with timestamps), batch embedding ingestion (CSV -> embeddings retention for 90 days), scheduled report export (report artifacts kept 14 days).

One ask: Marissa, can legal confirm the wording for "evidence bundle" and whether 30 days is ok for archive proof?

— Kim
Principal Security PM
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>

On Tue, 12 May 2026 at 10:21, Kimberly Park wrote:
> I'll prepare the scenario examples — interactive chat (demo conversation with timestamps), batch embedding ingestion (CSV -> embeddings retention for 90 days), scheduled report export (report artifacts kept 14 days).

FYI: legal is comfortable with the phraseology below (we can copy into the playbook):

"Evidence of deletion" = a signed statement and export showing the scope of objects targeted and timestamps of purge jobs. For live data this will be immediate (logical deletion + access tokens revoked). For backups/archives we provide a verification report when background purge completes; typical window 7–30 days depending on customer region and retention tier.

Concrete scenarios I suggest we include (short bullets + what the customer will see):
- Interactive chat (session ID: 1234): what we store by default — prompt, assistant replies, metadata (timestamp, model version), ephemeral streaming fragments (in-memory until end of session). Erasure result: session tokens removed from indexes; customer sees confirmation and receives proof PDF within 7 business days.
- Batch embeddings (upload.csv -> embeddings table): default store = vectors + minimal provenance (source filename, row id). Retention default = 90 days for pilot unless customer requests a shorter window. Erasure result: vectors removed from lookup indexes; we regenerate a deletion report referencing the original upload id.
- Scheduled report exports: final PDFs kept for 14 days by default, then auto-expire; if customer requests immediate removal we remove files from object storage and remove pointers from catalogs; proof delivered within 7 days.

I uploaded a draft to Drive: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1aB2cPlaybookDraft and attached a quick PDF draft to this thread (retention_playbook_draft.pdf).

Marissa
Lead, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: retention_playbook_draft.pdf]

Thanks team — this is helpful. A couple quick clarifying Qs from procurement/legal before we circulate internally:

1) For the "Batch embeddings" scenario: can you confirm whether provenance includes the original row content or just a row id? We need to verify PII is not retained.
2) For backups: we need clarity on whether backups are encrypted with our KMS or Redwood's, and whether the verification report includes KMS IDs.
3) Is there an SLA for delivering the deletion evidence bundle (we have a deadline of June 1 to confirm).

I've attached our data map so you can see the fields we send.

Best —
